entry_text:
Candidate-level integration requires a separate check. A prototype replaces
only selected \texttt{rfl} or \texttt{interval\_cases} tokens, retains the
surrounding submitted proof, and attempts a checked family theorem before
restoring state and invoking the original tactic on failure. One short
negative control reproduces the original diagnostics after normalizing only
file paths and removing measurement markers. That control does not establish
general fallback equivalence: the 49-source trial stops after 23 returns
because pending synthetic obligations can escape the new attempt.
Some logs print a certificate-hit marker before later unsolved goals and
\texttt{sorryAx} appear. A hit marker is therefore not acceptance; errors in
the transformed method are not certified rejections of the original candidate.
The retained partial proofs and budget interruptions supply no full-cohort
recovery rate, same-budget verdict parity or complete-service speedup.
Complete original-source differential and performance measurements remain open.
